notes:
I went through all 64 stations. Seven changed: Scurdie Ness, Isle of May, Monach Isles, Ushenish, Barra Head, Dubh Artach and Sanda. Holy Isle and Mull of Galloway I also marked as changed, with low confidence. The rest differ only in wording, or in sector bearings that are ¼ point apart or more precise; I take those to be re-surveyed or restated bearings, not changes a watcher at the station would see.

Things to check:
(1) Scurdie Ness: Edwards (March 1884) already says occulting, but Findlay 1887 dates the alteration 1885. I used 1885 and let the spans overlap 1884–85.
(2) Isle of May: no source dates the change to the 4-flash electric light. The witnesses allow 1884–86; check the commonly cited 1 Dec 1886 date, and whether the low light was put out in 1887 when the North Carr light-vessel came.
(3) Barra Head (3 min to 1 min) and Mull of Galloway (eclipse ½ min to ¼ min) have no date. Each could be a misprint in Findlay 1879; Barra Head's old pattern is the same as Tarbat Ness's. Check the scans.
(4) Isle Ornsay: Findlay 1879's 'br. or red' is word for word the Kyle Akin line above it. The other three witnesses say fixed white, so check p49r10.
(5) Chanonry Point: report1879 has 'revolving every minute' with red sectors, the same wording as its Covesea line. I followed Findlay and Edwards (fixed white).
(6) Holy Isle: the 1880 alteration seems to be a seasonal red pier light added. Decide whether that pier belongs to the station.
(7) Dubh Artach: only the inshore arc changed (red to occulting white), between 1880 and early 1884. Treat it as unchanged if you draw only the main arc.
(8) North Carr light-vessel and Ailsa Craig appear in the reports (1885–) before Findlay has them existing or lit (North Carr 'proposed' in 1887; Ailsa Craig lit 1886). Check the reports' own entries.
(9) Wharf and pier lights in Findlay 1887 (Stornoway item 3, Lerwick pier) are not the stations' own lights; don't draw them.
(10) Monach Isles (1882), Sanda (1882) and Ushenish (1885) are dated by Findlay 1887's alteration year, and Edwards agrees with each.
Findlay 1887 has no year column showing an alteration for Barra Head, Dubh Artach, Isle of May or Mull of Galloway, so those dates rest on the window between witnesses.
'latest' takes Findlay 1887 to reflect lights as of about 1886.
